refnamediv.refpurpose: Design an FIR filter using the window method.

refsynopsisdiv.title: Syntax
refsynopsisdiv.synopsis: b = fir1(n, w) b = fir1(n, w, type) b = fir1(n, w, type, window) b = fir1(n, w, type, window, noscale)

listitem.para: Normalized cutoff frequency or band edges (values between 0 and 1, where 1 corresponds to the Nyquist frequency).
Specifies the cutoff frequency for a lowpass or highpass filter.
Specifies the edges of a bandpass or bandstop filter.
Specifies the band edges for a multiband filter.
(optional) String specifying the filter type. Possible values are:
Lowpass filter (default if w is scalar).
Bandpass filter (default if w is a pair).
Multiband filter with the first band as a stopband (default if w has more than 2 elements).
Multiband filter with the first band as a passband.
(optional) Vector specifying the window to shape the filter. If not provided, a Hamming window is used by default.
(optional) If specified, the filter coefficients are not normalized. By default, the filter is normalized.
Vector containing the FIR filter coefficients.

refsection.title: Description
refsection.para: The `fir1` function designs an FIR filter of order `n` using the window method. The filter type and cutoff frequencies are specified by `w` and `type`. An optional window can be provided to shape the filter. By default, the filter coefficients are normalized to ensure a magnitude response of 1 at the center of the first passband.

- If the filter order `n` is odd and the final band is a passband, the order is incremented to avoid issues with the Nyquist frequency. - The periodic form of the window is used for spectral analysis, while the symmetric form is typically used for filter design.
